title: "Step 3: R primers"
subtitle: "Step 3 of 5"

**Time:** about 1 hour 50 minutes. Do 2 primers an evening.
**Before you start:** a web browser. Nothing to install.
**When you finish:** you have written R code and drawn a plot.

5 short pages. Each one has live code cells you edit and run inside the page.

Do them in order. Each page assumes the ones before it.

::: {.callout-important}
## Open these at home
The first page downloads about 17 MB. That is R itself, compiled to run in a
browser. Primer 5 draws plots and downloads about 37 MB.

Your browser keeps the download for 7 days. Work through these at home this
week and you pay nothing again at IISc.
:::

Primer 5 is the heavy one. Do it on a connection you trust.

## How to work through a primer

1. Open the page. Wait for the cells to become ready.
2. Press **Run** on every cell, from the top down.
3. Change a number in a cell and press **Run** again.
4. Do each exercise. Press **Hint** before you press **Solution**.

**You should see:** output under each cell after you press Run, and a green
tick when an exercise is correct.

**If it does not work:** see the next section.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this matters
Reading code teaches you very little. The cells exist so that you type, get an
error, and fix it, before Monday rather than during a session.

Nothing carries from one page to the next. Each page starts R from scratch.
:::

## If the cells never become ready

Wait 2 or 3 minutes first. The page has to download R before anything runs.

**If it still does not work:**

1. Try a phone hotspot. Hospital and institutional wifi often block this.
2. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
3. Turn off any ad blocker for this site.
4. Use the [R primer reference](r-primer.qmd) in RStudio instead. It teaches
   the same material.

There is no Stop button on these pages. If you write a loop that never ends,
reload the page.
